prompt: I want to modify the end-to-end flow related to the program IMM102S. Count and list all the database tables that can be impacted by this change.

count.description: Exact number of distinct database tables found.

tables.description: The distinct table names counted, by exact name.

justification.description: Which files, copybooks, or SQL statements were inspected to arrive at this count.

prompt: I want to modify the EMP table. Count and list all the COBOL programs that can be directly impacted by this change.

count.description: Exact number of distinct COBOL programs found.

programs.description: The distinct program file names counted, by exact file name (e.g. 'COBASV01.COB').

justification.description: Which SQL statements, cursors, or copybooks were inspected to arrive at this count.

prompt: I'm planning to change the internal behavior of the subprogram IMMDATES (the number and types of parameters stay identical, only the logic changes). List all calls in the code that specifically invoke this subprogram -- including calls made indirectly through a variable or field that holds the program name at runtime, not only literal CALL 'IMMDATES' statements. For each call, specify the file and whether the call is literal or made through a named field.

count.description: Exact number of distinct files containing a call to IMMDATES, literal or indirect.

files.description: Distinct file names (e.g. 'IMM0038.COB') containing a call to IMMDATES.

call_style.description: 'literal' for CALL 'IMMDATES', or 'indirect' for a call through a named field/variable.

justification.description: Which files/copybooks were inspected to arrive at this list, and how indirect calls were resolved.

prompt: I'm planning to change the internal behavior of the subprogram IMMEIEIO (the number and types of parameters stay identical, only the logic changes). Before I touch anything, I need the full impact footprint of this change: 1) every COBOL program that directly calls IMMEIEIO; 2) every database table that IMMEIEIO itself directly reads from or writes to. For each calling program, name the file. For each table, confirm it is touched by IMMEIEIO's own SQL statements (not a table touched by one of its callers).

calling_programs.description: Distinct COBOL program file names that directly call IMMEIEIO.

tables.description: Database tables read from or written to directly inside IMMEIEIO.

justification.description: Call sites and SQL statements used as evidence for this list.

prompt: I'm planning to change how the MEMBERSHIP IMS database (DBDNAME IMMMBRDB, PSB IMM0038, the 3rd PCB declared in that PSB, PROCOPT=AP) is accessed. List every COBOL paragraph across the entire codebase that performs a DL/I call (GU, GHU, GN, GHN, ISRT, DLET, REPL, or any CBLTDLI-based call) specifically against this PCB. This PCB has no literal name in the source that spells it out directly -- programs bind to it positionally through the PSB's PCB order, and build the PCB mask from the generic IMMDBPCB copybook (COPY IMMDBPCB REPLACING ==(DBDNME)== BY ==...==) using an arbitrary replacement name that is NOT 'IMMMBRDB'. Do not include: (a) paragraphs that only declare a PCB mask without ever issuing a DL/I call against it, (b) paragraphs whose DL/I calls target a different PCB/database built from the same generic IMMDBPCB copybook.

count.description: Exact number of distinct paragraphs found performing a DL/I call against this specific PCB.

paragraphs.description: Distinct paragraph names (format 'File.COB::PARAGRAPH-NAME') performing a DL/I call against this specific PCB.

justification.description: How the PSB/PCB positional binding was resolved (which PSB, which PCB position, which copybook expansion) and which files were inspected as evidence.

notes: Strongest case found in this project so far: a literal grep for CAST's own synthesized object name for this PCB ('IMM0038-03-IMMMBRDB-AP') returns ZERO hits anywhere in the source (confirmed 2026-08-27) -- that string never appears as text, it's derived from the PCB's position within the PSB, which a COBOL program binds to only positionally via its DL/I ENTRY linkage, not by name. Independently verified the underlying mechanism by direct source read: IMS/PSB/IMM0038.PSB declares 'PCB TYPE=DB,DBDNAME=IMMMBRDB,KEYLEN=27,PROCOPT=AP' as the 3rd PCB entry (no PCB index number appears in the PSB text either); COBOL/PROGRAMS/IMM0038.COB (lines ~2810-2834) builds multiple PCB masks from the same generic COBOL/COPYBOOKS/IMMDBPCB.CPY copybook via COPY...REPLACING with names like IMMMBR2DB/IMMMBR3DB/IMMMBR4DB -- none of which spell IMMMBRDB. The expected count of 65 is CAST Imaging's own self-reported structural dependent count (from a CAST-Imaging-assisted exploration session, not independently re-derived here) -- by construction, independently reconstructing this exact count via grep/text search is not practically feasible, which is the entire point of this question. The full list of 65 paragraph names has NOT been captured yet, so score-results.py can currently only check 'count' (via count_correct), not the 'paragraphs' array (acc/noise will show as unscored/0 until the full list is added to 'expected').
